name: Newsletter
description: Subscribers and campaigns for the shop's news and offers: a subscription block the shop lays out in its own HTML, a form under the basket, a tick at checkout, a switch in the customer's account, every address confirmed by a letter (double opt-in). Campaigns with product cards go to every subscriber or to a segment, in each reader's language, at the pace the mail server allows, with opens and clicks counted; every letter has its way out. The list also exports for an outside mailing service, and subscribers are in the shop's personal-data registry.

permissions.name: newsletter.manage
permissions.label: See, export and import newsletter subscribers, send campaigns

keywords.en: newsletter campaign mailing email blast send letter

settings.label: Confirm every address by a letter
settings.help: A new subscriber is counted only after following the link in the letter. Off, anybody's address can be put on the list by anybody — and mailing services and the law in many countries ask for the confirmation. A signed-in customer whose address is already confirmed is not asked again.

settings.label: Offer to subscribe on the basket page
settings.help: A small form under the basket.

settings.label: A "Subscribe to news and offers" tick at checkout
settings.help: The order's email is subscribed when the tick is on — and confirmed by a letter like any other.

settings.label: The checkout tick is on from the start
settings.help: Off is the honest default: a tick put there for the customer is not their consent, and in the EU it is not consent at all.

settings.label: Campaign letters per minute
settings.help: How fast a campaign goes out. A mail server sent too much at once starts refusing, and the provider marks the shop as a spammer: ask yours what it allows (a shared hosting box often allows 100–300 an hour, a mailing service thousands a minute).

settings.label: Link to the privacy policy
settings.help: Shown beside the subscription form as {privacy_link}. Empty — no link.
